name: phys-selection-lows
title: Physics backend selection follow-ups (J2/J3 lows): the Deterministic preset refuses to start until the backend implements layers/triggers/events/queries, a Jolt-only build selects Jolt by default, ChooseBackend checks PhysX is built, correct wording when the Jolt request comes from the host option, physics.html Not-verified callout
issue: Follow-up of the merged Jolt J2 (#199) and J3 (#205) PRs; the user accepted these LOW findings as a follow-up. Design C:/Method Notes Obsidian/orchestrator/proposals/physics-backend-investigation-156.md sections 4.2 and 6.3. Verify each against master first. (1) engine/src/network/NetworkValidation.cpp (~line 87): the Deterministic preset currently STARTS on Jolt (strict-FP build, physics.deterministic on) although Jolt's triggers, layers, contact/trigger events and queries are not implemented yet (J4/J5): add to IPhysicsBackend a declared set of implemented feature groups (layers/matrix, triggers, contact+trigger events, queries; PhysX declares all; JoltBackend declares only what exists on master) and make the Deterministic preset validation REFUSE to start (clear error naming the missing groups and the backend) unless every group is implemented; tests for refusal and acceptance (use a fake backend declaring all groups for the acceptance path); (2) engine/src/Application.cpp (~line 394) and engine/include/engine/physics/PhysicsBackendKind.hpp ChooseBackend (~line 383): in a build with N2ENGINE_USE_JOLT=ON and N2ENGINE_USE_PHYSX=OFF a project without physics.backend gets NO physics because the default/fallback is always PhysX; and ChooseBackend falls back to PhysX without checking PhysX is built (the warning says 'using physx instead' when nothing will start). New rule: AUTO/unset selects PhysX when built, else Jolt when built, else none; any fallback names only a backend that is compiled in; if the requested backend is unavailable and no other is built, a clear refusal message; unit tests for every build-flag combination the selection function can see (make it testable without the real flags, e.g. pass availability in); (3) engine/src/Application.cpp (~line 160): when the Jolt request comes from the host's ApplicationOptions (no project setting), the fallback/refusal message and the Physics health row still say 'physics.backend is jolt': name the actual source (host option vs project setting); (4) docs/physics.html (~line 444): the Jolt 'Not verified' callout says cross-leg hash equality is unverified, but JoltBackendDeterminismTest asserts the golden constants on every leg and docs/testing.html tabulates equal hashes: correct it to what is and is not verified. Update docs/physics.html, docs/netcode.html (Deterministic preset requirements) and docs/application.html where the selection text changes. Record the new default rule for Jolt-only builds as a deviation for the user. Nothing builds locally for the engine; CI (12 checks) is the test; expect fix rounds; re-read every edit twice (CMake/YAML/C++ syntax); NEVER call a stateful function (RNG etc.) twice in one argument list or operator expression (unspecified evaluation order); NEVER run taskkill or kill other processes; verify every docs sentence against the CODE; no attribution lines on commits or PRs (no Co-Authored-By, no Generated-with footer); GitHub only via the wrapper; before your final push merge origin/master into the branch if it moved (other Jolt items run in parallel: resolve conflicts keeping both sides); your FINAL message must be a real report (PR number, head sha, what you did, deviations), never a single word.
acceptance: Deterministic preset refuses while the backend lacks any feature group; tested
Selection: PhysX if built else Jolt else none; fallbacks only to built backends; source-aware messages; tested
notes: Reviewer: every build-flag combination, the refusal cannot be bypassed by the host option, messages name the right source, docs true.
